#2572. 49ers return to winning ways coming off bye week: Winners, losers vs Raiders

The San Francisco 49ers were fresh off their bye week and it showed with a 38-17 Week 9 win, a completely dominant outing against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California.

The Niners improved to 7-1 behind a stellar defensive performance that forced the Raiders into five turnovers and held their run game to 24 total yards.

Offensively, the 49ers looked like they picked up where they left off. Despite playing without wideouts Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel Sr. and Christian Kirk, they found a way to keep their offense explosive and rolling.

Quarterback Brock Purdy completed 17-of-25 passes and threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns, eclipsing his 100th career passing touchdown. He also ran for 40 yards and touchdown, as his game continues to give MVP considerations.

"It's been amazing. Just since the first game he got in there," Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Brock's been the man since he's come in and that's a pretty unbelievable deal considering where he was drafted, how he started. Very fortunate to have Brock."

32 THINGS WE LEARNED: QB crises testing teams as backups flounder

Running back Christian McCaffrey tied Hall of Famer Joe Perry for most consecutive games with a rushing touchdown. It was McCaffrey's seventh straight score. He had 18 carries for 68 yards. He added two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown.

The game featured a historic rivalry between two franchises that were once separated by the Bay Bridge. When the Raiders were located in Oakland, it made for the one of the best regional rivalries in sports. Although it's not the same since the Raiders moved to Vegas, it will always be revered by the fans as such.

With Sunday's win, the 49ers took a 9-7 all-time advantage against the Raiders. Here are winners and losers from the matchup:

The 49ers defense forced three turnovers in 3rd quarter, alone. San Francisco forced Las Vegas into an interception by rookie Jaden Dugger who took it back 35 yards for a touchdown on the first drive of the second half. Their two forced fumbles were caused by Fred Warner and Upton Stout.

"That was honestly the emphasis going into this week," Warner said. "I think we just had a spurt where there was a drought in takeaways, and we know how important that is to winning football games and for our team moving forward. ... to come out in the second half and have five of those was unbelievable. It was honestly just guys being in the right spot, doing their job, playing relentlessly, getting to the football and having it on their mind. So, it was definitely a point of emphasis."

Defensive edge Nick Bosa returned from a five-game absence nursing back from knee and calf injuries. DeForest Buckner returned to the 49ers after being traded by the Indianapolis Colts. Each had a tackle, but it's their presence that has things feeling nostalgic for San Francisco.

"Those are two super disruptive players for our D-line, and the offense has to have a plan for them at all times," Warner said. "It frees up a lot of things for the rest of the defense. Of course, I've got to go back and watch the film to really see just how big of an impact they had. But, I mean, you can't not be happy with the fact that we have both of them out on the field for us going forward."

Buckner said he's home again. He was the last name called during their starting lineup introductions. Warner told him to go last.

"It felt great, you know what I mean? Being able to go out there with those guys and fly around on defense, I mean, you could just feel the energy," Buckner said. "You got to fly around to the ball to go make plays, and that's the fun part about it. Not only competing with the Raiders, but with your fellow teammates, because everybody's hungry to make plays."

This just felt necessary to point out that Warner's signature punch out caused so many fumbles. Warner had one, and the fumble that Stout caused to save a touchdown was exactly how Warner would have done it himself.

Jordan Watkins finally had the breakout game that he's capable of. Watkins put up four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown.

"A huge step forward," Shanahan said. "He hasn't gotten his opportunities and some guys have been down andhe's been working and he's been ready for it. I think he's gotten better each week. I think the first week he came out there and played good right away. The ball went his way more this game and he was ready for those opportunities. I thought he's blocked well and stuff. One penalty he'd like to take back, but we can forgive him. That third down was huge. Just the man coverage and going up and making that play on the post. That was a hell of a play."

You can credit the 49ers defense if you want, but the Raiders' run game was nonexistent. Ashton Jeanty, the former No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, had just 25 yards on six touches.

#2571. Observations after well-balanced Sixers hold off Bulls

Observations after well-balanced Sixers hold off Bulls originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

Still no losing streaks to speak of for the 2026-27 Sixers.

The Sixers earned a 127-121 win Sunday over the Bulls to wrap up a 2-1 road trip. They moved to 9-2 overall and Chicago fell to 1-8.

Every Sixers starter scored in double figures.

Three reached the 20-point mark in Jaylen Brown (29 points), Tyrese Maxey (27 points) and LeBron James (22). Joel Embiid had 18 points and 10 rebounds.

Josh Giddey posted 19 points, 15 assists and seven rebounds for the Bulls.

The Sixers were without Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Bulls' absences included Norman Powell (right shoulder inflammation/soreness) and Zach Collins (respiratory illness).

Next on the Sixers' schedule is a home game Tuesday night vs. the Celtics. Here are observations on their win over Chicago:

Following his 0-for-9 night Friday in the Sixers' loss to the Cavaliers, Embiid did not snap right back into form.

He was well short on his first shot attempt, a wide-open three-pointer. Embiid then failed to score in the post over Jalen Smith.

Embiid got a field goal to go at the 6:42 mark of the first quarter when he tipped in his own miss. However, Smith canned a three on the ensuing possession to give Chicago a 23-16 lead.

James committed two early turnovers, although he did sink a corner three-pointer during a fast-paced first quarter. VJ Edgecombe added two long-range jumpers in the first.

Entering Sunday, the Sixers' minus-9.6 net rating in the first quarter ranked 27th in the NBA. They managed to hold a one-point lead in Chicago after the first.

The Sixers' offensive rebounding was their greatest strength in the first quarter. They poured in 17 second-chance points. Embiid had four offensive boards in the opening frame.

Jabari Walker assumed backup center duties for the second straight game without Bona. He picked up where Embiid left off on the glass, grabbing seven rebounds (three offensive) in a great first stint.

Though he's undersized in the height department for an NBA center at 6-foot-7, Walker has plenty of rebounding tools.

He's listed at a strong 237 pounds, doesn't mind contact whatsoever, hunts the ball, and has a knack for winning contested boards. Walker showed all of that Sunday. Very hard to overstate how well he rebounded.

The Sixers' first-shot offense also had many bright moments in the second quarter.

James got rolling on his way to a 16-point first half, Embiid made a couple of mid-range jumpers, and Maxey hit two free throws put the Sixers up 60-50 late in the second period.

Chicago evened the game at 68-all early in the third quarter on a Matas Buzelis three, but the Bulls couldn't sustain that run.

The Bulls' defense continued to look like one of the worst in the NBA and the Sixers' well-balanced offense kept the scoreboard moving. Brown nailed a turnaround jumper to give his team a double-digit lead. Walker knocked down a top-of-the-key triple to extend the Sixers' advantage to 12 points.

The Sixers had two apparent injury scares in the second half. Brown limped to the sideline with 6:55 to go in the third quarter, but he stayed in the game. Edgecombe headed to the locker room after subbing out at the 9:08 mark of the fourth quarter. He returned to the Sixers' bench and ultimately returned for a final stint.

On the floor, the Sixers couldn't ease to victory. Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson trimmed Chicago's deficit to 116-113 by draining a three. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse called timeout.

The Sixers were efficient enough in the half court down the stretch.

Embiid made a put-back hoop and a pair of free throws. Maxey drilled a side-step three-ball after a wraparound feed from James. The Sixers converted their clutch free throws and secured a winning road trip.

#2567. Shavkat Rakhmonov Pushes Back Against Fresh Knee Injury Reports, Hints at UFC Return in Early 2027

There is some rare good news for Shavkat Rakhmonov fans. The undefeated Kazakh was recently rumored to have suffered another knee setback. However, he has now pushed back against those reports, suggesting that his return might be closer than expected.

For the unversed, several Russian media outlets recently reported that Rakhmonov had aggravated his existing knee injury, potentially delaying his comeback even further. One of the reports claimed, "Knee cannot withstand strain."

The 19-0 contender was previously expected to face Michael Morales at UFC 336 before the latter was booked for the interim welterweight title fight. Following the injury reports, speculation suggested that Rakhmonov might not return until June 2027. However, the Kazakh's latest updates paint a much more positive picture.

In a new post on his X account, Rakhmonov wrote, "Another week of hard training done. Getting stronger every single day." He also shared a separate update on Instagram with an encouraging caption: "Soon 2027."

ALSO READ: Donald Trump Reveals Dana White Press Secretary Offer Was a Joke, But Still Likes the Idea

That's certainly good news considering the difficult couple of years the 19-0 contender has endured. Rakhmonov hasn't competed since his victory over Ian Garry at UFC 310 in December 2024.

The bout was originally supposed to be against then-champion Belal Muhammad for the welterweight title. However, Muhammad was forced to withdraw due to a bone infection, leaving Garry to step in on short notice.

Despite dealing with existing ACL and meniscus problems, Rakhmonov managed to grind out a decision victory over the Irishman. However, the damage to his knee reportedly worsened during the fight, with Garry repeatedly targeting his injured left leg.

Rakhmonov initially explored conservative treatment through rest and rehabilitation before eventually undergoing surgery on January 31, 2026. At the time, his recovery was expected to take approximately nine to 10 months.

Since then, several clips have shown the Kazakh gradually working his way back into training. He has been focusing on conditioning and has even participated in sparring sessions. Still, questions remained about how soon he could realistically return to competition.

Back in May 2026, his manager, Daniel Rubenstein, revealed that the early prognosis suggested the former title challenger might not be ready to fight until 2027.

Although the lengthy recovery has been frustrating for fans, Rakhmonov's latest updates offer some much-needed optimism. If his progress continues at this pace, the undefeated contender could finally be on his way back to the Octagon without another major setback.

#2565. Justin Herbert has a possible fracture in his left middle finger

Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert left Sunday’s game in the fourth quarter.

The game was out of hand, but the bigger issue is Herbert’s hand.

Coach Jim Harbaugh said postgame that he made the decision to pull Herbert after an injury to Herbert’s left middle finger.

“It could be a fracture,” Harbaugh said, via Alex Insdorf of Bolt Breakdowns. “We’ll find out.”

Herbert appeared to injure his non-throwing hand on a sack by Logan Hall when the quarterback tried to stiff-arm the defensive lineman with 14:12 remaining. Herbert, who was sacked eight times in the 44-22 loss, threw a touchdown pass two plays later.

Harbaugh said Herbert wanted to stay in the game.

Herbert had his left hand surgically repaired during the 2025 season after breaking a bone in the back of the hand during a Week 13 game. He played through the injury and expects to play through his current injury.

“I’ll do whatever I can to make sure I’m 100 percent,” Herbert said after the game.

Herbert will undergo further testing on Monday.

#2564. Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup

Observations after Sixers suffer blowout loss to Cavs, fall in NBA Cup originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia

The Sixers couldn't rekindle the magic of their comeback home-opening win over the Cavaliers.

They fell Friday night in NBA Cup action, suffering a 119-95 defeat in Cleveland. The Sixers dipped to 8-2 and the Cavs improved to 5-4.

The Sixers' top scorers were Jaylen Brown (20 points), VJ Edgecombe (19 points) and Tyrese Maxey (17).

The Cavs got 23 points from Donovan Mitchell and 22 from Evan Mobley.

The Sixers' injured players included center Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain). Cleveland was down big man Jarrett Allen (right knee contusion). Sam Merrill sat out the second half with a right elbow injury.

With Friday's loss, the Sixers are 1-1 in Eastern Conference Group B of the NBA Cup. Their next Cup game is scheduled for Nov. 25 against the Heat.

The Sixers will conclude their three-road trip Sunday afternoon against the Bulls. Here are observations on their blowout loss to Cleveland:

After a missed Merrill three-pointer, the Sixers steamed ahead on the fast break and Edgecombe opened the scoring with a slam.

The Cavs replied with a 15-0 run kickstarted by six straight Mitchell points. Much like in the Sixers' Oct. 22 win over Cleveland, they were many levels below their best in the first quarter.

The Sixers began 0 for 4 from three-point range, including two LeBron James misses. The Cavs were also the better team in transition and limited the Sixers' chances to attack in the open floor by taking excellent care of the ball in the early going. Edgecombe was called for his second foul with 7:34 left in the first quarter.

Meanwhile, Joel Embiid expressed his frustration about a couple of early no-calls. Embiid's larger problem was that he couldn't hit any sort of shot besides free throws.

He went 0 for 9 from the floor in the game. The seven-time All-Star finished with six points and seven rebounds.

Embiid has had a subpar shooting start to the year, especially from three-point territory — he's now 3 for 28 (10.7 percent) — but Friday was the kind of extreme night that's bound to happen here and there over the course of a long season.

Of course, it's notable that Embiid's been playing through right foot plantar fasciitis and the Sixers have been keeping a close eye on his minutes. We'll see how the team manages his availability moving forward and whether Embiid is able to bounce back next time out.

James didn't play anywhere near his finest game either. He had eight points on 3-for-12 shooting, eight rebounds, three assists and six turnovers.

As a team, the Sixers were 36.5 percent from the field and 25 percent beyond the arc.

Jabari Walker rejoined the Sixers' rotation as the backup center with Bona sidelined. Anfernee Simons, former Cav Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope all remained rotation fixtures.

With Walker and Caldwell-Pope on the court next to three starters, the Sixers cut their deficit to single digits in the second quarter. Walker threw down a fast-break dunk that cut Cleveland's lead to 48-41. He gave the Sixers some good defensive possessions when switched on to James Harden and provided his usual physical, high-effort work on the glass.

Edgecombe was fantastic in the second, sinking three triples, racking up 15 points and nabbing three steals.

Many second-year players would have a tough time finding a rhythm after encountering early foul trouble, but Edgecombe was great as soon as he checked back in and delivered a ton of valuable buckets in the Sixers' comeback push.

The Sixers pulled to within 66-63 when Maxey picked a steal and threw a pretty one-handed bounce pass to Edgecombe for a dunk.

With Embiid and James offering little as scorers, Brown hit several shots that helped the Sixers stay in the game. After his 30-point performance last time out against the Pistons, Brown reached the 20-point mark for a third consecutive game.

Still, the Sixers' offense never got rolling. The Cavs maintained their lead and extended it late in the third quarter. By early in the fourth, the Sixers trailed by over 20 points.

Embiid didn't play the fourth quarter and logged 25 minutes. He's had zero made field goals on just one other occasion in his career, back in Nov. 2019 against the Raptors.

Even with their tremendous first nine games, the Sixers knew they'd hit speed bumps throughout the year. They'll try to get back on track Sunday in Chicago.

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert hasn't had a year worth remembering through the first eight games.

#2548. Fantasy Football Week 9 RB Report: Breece Hall returns for Jets, sends Braelon Allen back to secondary role

Welcome back for another edition of the fantasy football running back report. In Week 9, we have a few important backfields to highlight and break down for fantasy on a pretty lackluster Sunday afternoon overall for fantasy scoring, particularly at the RB position. While the fantasy points weren't flowing, there's still enough that we can gather to help inform us in our lineup decisions moving forward.

Let's dive in on some committee backfields and what to make of them as we approach Week 10.

Hall was back after missing the past five games due to a quad injury. In his stead, Allen had filled in admirably, putting up top-10 RB fantasy numbers from Weeks 4-8. Over that stretch, Allen averaged 15.2 fantasy points per game in half-PPR formats. He had four straight games with double-digit fantasy points going into Week 9. If you were fortunate enough to snag Allen, you were living a fantasy manager's dream.

But things came crashing down to earth in Week 9 against the Chiefs. We expected Hall to retain his lead-back role with Allen mixing in, keeping a role in the offense, albeit lesser than when Hall was out. But it wasn't exactly the 50-50 split we thought it would be, as Hall out-touched Allen, 18-10. Neither back went wild for managers given the tough road matchup against Kansas City. That will play a big factor in how we evaluate this backfield.

I'm willing to chalk this up to being a poor game script and situation for both backs. The Jets offense struggled to move the ball and it was probably a gift Hall and Allen got to those fantasy totals. New York also wanted to work Hall back up to speed while keeping Allen involved. WR Garrett Wilson (concussion) being out also doesn't help the unit overall.

So if we look ahead to Week 10 against the Bills, it should be easier for the Jets to move the ball. If Wilson is back, that could take some opportunities away in the passing game from each back. If Hall maintains this volume, he'll be a low-end RB2/3. Allen is more of a flex play at this point but is worth keeping on your roster in case something happens to Hall again.

We may have to graduate the Broncos' backfield out of this series now that Coleman has taken things over. But we do have to see how the splits go once RB RJ Harvey is off injured reserve. Until then, it appears to be Coleman's job and Dobbins continues to fall further out of favor with head coach Sean Payton.

Coleman wasn't very efficient with his touches, but it was clear we were going to get a response from the Panthers' defense after DC Ejiro Evero was fired following the loss last week on TNF to the Packers. So with Todd Wash taking over the defense, there was an emphasis on stopping the run given what we've seen from Denver's passing game.

Even so, Coleman was able to get home and is trending toward an RB1 finish with 16.8 fantasy points. He commanded most of the RB touches and scored a key TD in the red zone in the second half. The Broncos head into the bye in Week 10, so Coleman will be out of service. They'll face the Raiders in Week 11, Coleman will be a very strong RB2 play in that contest. Denver also has a great schedule down the stretch and one could assume Coleman, as a rookie, will only get better with more reps.

We just need to hope that the eventual return of Harvey doesn't cut into Coleman's workload too much. There's a chance Harvey retains the passing-down role while Coleman handles most of the ground work and goal-line carries. That would still make him very valuable for fantasy but limit his ceiling a bit.

As the NFL Trade Deadline looms on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET, it appears the Colts are going to hold onto Taylor. But the way the offense has been deploying the running backs the past few weeks, it's looking like this could be more of a committee the rest of 2026. The Colts could make a few more moves before the deadline to position themselves for additional draft picks. With the playoffs not on the menu this season, Indy wants to get a look at McGowan, who scored his first NFL touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys.

Taylor still got most of the work but failed to get to double-digit fantasy points for a second straight week. JT was also had some bad luck. He was taken out of the game on 3rd-and-goal because he lost his shoe, which allowed McGowan to score.

This is a tough situation. In a perfect world, Taylor gets traded to a contender and is in a much better environment for fantasy. With Indianapolis not playing for anything, it's unlikely Taylor gets his usual touch volume moving forward as McGowan could continue to see more looks.

I think JT will have some games where the Colts let him run wild and he gets home for fantasy managers. But the organization also doesn't care about your fantasy team. Taylor is less of an RB1 and more of an RB2 with upside who could continue to trend in the wrong direction. It may be tough to start him later in the season once the fantasy playoffs roll around, too.

McGowan is looking like a fringe flex option, but a player who could slowly see his role increase if he continues to be efficient with his runs. The rookie isn't a bad stash off the waiver wire going into Week 10, depending on what happens at the deadline on Tuesday.

The Seahawks got Charb back in the lineup last week, the first time he was on the field since tearing his ACL last season. He was eased back into action with just nine touches while playing 23 snaps (37%). George Holani saw 11 snaps last week as well, while rookie Jadarian Price played the most with 48%. But we saw a clear shift in Week 9.

Charbonnet got the bulk of the ground work while Price was the receiving back. The AJ Barner goal-line TD is frustrating, but other than that, this is an encouraging sign for managers of both backs, really. The Seahawks didn't need much to get past the lowly Cardinals and let the defense carry them.

For Charbonnet, this script is good news. Sam Darnold was out and the passing game took a bit of a hit with Drew Lock under center. That's concerning in that it could mean Seattle's drives stall out more often against tougher opponents. It would hurt Price's stock since we'd see Jaxon Smith-Njigba much more involved than Sunday (7-51 on 10 targets).

If you have Charb, he's looking like he could pay off late in the season after being a stash for the first half. Even if he isn't particularly explosive, he'll eat up carries and should see goal-line touches. Charbonnet is working his way into the RB2 convo but is more of an RB3/flex play at the moment. Price is more volatile but could provide decent flex value in PPR formats and would need to step up if anything happens to Charb.

#2543. LIVE DISCUSSION: Brooklyn Nets at Dallas Mavericks, 7:30 PM ET

There was a time not so long ago when the Brooklyn Nets were among the teams hoping to land Cooper Flagg. I even spotted one optimist on the Long Island Rail Road wearing DIY jerseys celebrating that very possibility after the 2024 NBA Draft.

That pipe dream turned into a miracle for the Dallas Mavericks, a team that contended for a play-in spot, fell into the lottery, then landed the No.1 overall pick after having a 1.8% chance at it. There's no denying Brooklyn's disappointment when the pick fell the No.8, but Egor Dëmin has seen his own success early in his career for fans to at least feel good.

Sunday will be a stark reminder of where the Nets are. They're 2-7, they've dropped 118 games in the prior two years, and Houston is holding their pick. Rebuilding is one thing, compounding it with avoidable self-inflicted wounds is another. This is a young team and it's a long season, but you play to win the game.

They played on Saturday night and lost a game that they should've won. Point blank. Nolan Traore has been playing like a star and it continued with 19 points against Atlanta, but Jordi Fernandez benched him the entire fourth quarter.

"Mikel had those five straight points, and I just let him roll," Fernandez said after the game. "Because you cannot just keep taking them in and out. I think that when I was about to sub Nolan in, Mikel made two or three threes and a mid-range pull-up. So I thought that was the right thing to do. Was it right? I don't know. Obviously, Nolan did very well. They scored 18 and 19. So that's a very good contribution from your two point guards."

Perhaps the strangest part in it all? They're only one game out from a play-in spot. Mikel Brown Jr. is sitting this one out (back-to-back) alongside Egor Dëmin (bone bruise).

On the other side, Cooper Flagg, Kyrie Irving and the 5-4 Mavericks are coming off a 112-100 win over the Utah Jazz in NBA Cup play Friday night.

Where: American Airlines Center, Dallas, TX

OUT: Tarik Biberovic (right heel bursitis)

OUT: Dereck Lively II (right foot surgery)

OUT: Sergio de Larrea (right knee sprain)

"If they want to win, they'll need to slow down an old friend. Kyrie Irving is back after missing last year with an ACL tear. He's averaging 21 points a night and the shooting splits are quality enough, but HOW he's getting his buckets are a bit different than what we're used to. His field goal attempts inside of three feet are at the lowest mark of his career and his three point rate is at the highest of his career. Chances are that'll change the further he gets away from the injury, but it's certainly something to keep an eye on. #2540. 5 moments that defined the Patriots’ loss to the Packers

The New England Patriots were thoroughly beaten by the Green Bay Packers on Sunday afternoon, losing with a final score of 45-27 at Gillette Stadium. The game was a lopsided affair from start to finish, with the team home falling behind 17-0 quickly and never recovering.

Here is a Patriots-centric view at some of those key moments from the Week 9 contest.

The Patriots started the ball on offense, and it took them only two plays to give it away again. On a 2nd-and-9, Drake Maye maneuvered the pocket and attempted to hit Mack Hollins on a floater across his body. The ball, however, didn't land close to his intended targeted and instead was picked off by Xavier McKinney. The Packers safety went on to return the interception all the way to the New England 9-yard line.

Despite being early in the contest, the play was the biggest one of the afternoon in terms of expected points added: it resulted in a 5.9-point swing in Green Bay's favor. Two plays after the INT, the Packers took a 7-0 lead.

The Patriots defense started in a losing position, meaning that its first drive wasn't necessarily cause for concern yet. The second was, however, because it showed the Packers doing exactly what they had been doing all year: threatening teams with their deep passing game.

The first of seven explosive plays gained 49 yards, with Matthew Golden finding an opening against the Patriots' zone coverage and Kevin Byard being unable to close it in time. It was a sign of things to come.

The Patriots showed little resistance early on, and found themselves trailing 17-0 in the early second quarter. At that point, they finally got their act together and on a 3rd-and-10 found the end zone for the first time. Drake Maye's touchdown pass to Rhamondre Stevenson on a wheel route was well executed by both, and finally gave New England some momentum.

Finally starting to play some complementary football, the Patriots were in prime position to turn the game into a one-score contest again midway through the second period. They failed to do so: after driving into Green Bay territory on the very next possession after the Stevenson touchdown, Drake Maye was intercepted by Xavier McKinney for a second time and a third time overall in the game.

Instead of the Patriots further building on their momentum, the pick thwarted a prime opportunity and allowed Green Bay to score a touchdown just three plays later.

The Patriots entered the locker room at the half trailing by 10 points — a sizable deficit, but not one they couldn't overcome if they showed some improvement in the third quarter. Unfortunately, that is precisely what they did not do. Their defense continued to struggle against the big play on the opening series of the third quarter, and allowed Green Bay to march right back into the red zone.

Holding the Packers to a field goal at that point would have been a success and some much-needed damage limitation. That didn't happen, and a touchdown on 3rd-and-7 very gave the visitors a comforting 17-point lead again.

#2534. Sixers Bell Ringer: Offense carries Sixers as they hang on vs. Bulls

Bell Ringer Standings:Tyrese Maxey – 3.5VJ Edgecombe – 2Jaylen Brown – 1.5Joel Embiid – 1LeBron James – 1Anfernee Simons – 1

The bad news is the Sixers' defense looked like that of a veteran team closing a road trip with a Sunday afternoon game.

The good news is the offense was balanced and had bright spots in a 127-121 win over the Bulls in Chicago Sunday. The Sixers still hold the best record in the NBA at 9-2 and are 5-1 on the road to start the season.

The Bulls shot 52.3% from the field and were down one possession at multiple times late, but Jaylen Brown and the Sixers seemed to come away with big buckets and big stops when they desperately needed them.

Next up, the Sixers welcome Jayson Tatum and the Boston Celtics to town Tuesday night. No word if there will be any lamb chops and gravy served at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

Tyrese Maxey: 27 points, 7 assists, 4 rebounds

Nick Nurse mixed up the way he staggered his starters Sunday, opting to give Maxey an extended look with the second unit. There were nice moments, but some struggles as well. Playing Maxey more with Joel Embiid seemed to help both players. Embiid didn't have his most efficient night, but he was much better than he was in Cleveland.

It felt like an easy 27 points for Maxey, who seemed to take nothing but threes and shots at the rim. He tried to send Josh Giddey into the shadow realm with a dunk, but was fouled. He hit a big triple down the stretch off a ridiculous LeBron pass.

And, of course, he was a blur in transition.

Jaylen Brown: 29 points, 7 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal

Brown was excellent throughout this game. The way he attacks downhill with physicality has to be such a welcome sight for Sixers fans. His ability to make tough fallaways in the paint is elite. The footwork on this play is an example of what the ability to make those short fadeaways opens up.

This was another game where Brown simply made winning plays down the stretch. He made a couple big threes as the Sixers were leaking oil midway through the fourth. He also made four free throws and turned Giddey over in the final minute.

And two more stats: Brown had just one turnover and was a +8. Take that, nerds.

LeBron James: 22 points, 5 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal

Coming off his worst game as a Sixer against the Cavs, James didn't get off to a great start with a couple early turnovers. His second stint started with him settling for a midrange jumper while being guarded by Giddey.

From there, James stopped messing around.

LeBron was much more aggressive getting downhill, either finding teammates or finishing at the rim. It's crazy that at 41 he can still take over games for extended stretches.

I know he's played for a million years, but passes like this are still stunning.

An honorable mention here for Walker who's done a commendable job filling in for Adem Bona at the five. While there were sleepy moments throughout the day for the Sixers, Walker did what he always does — hustled, crashed the glass and brought energy.

He's been popping up here as an honorable mention on what feels like a nightly basis. At this point, he should be in a competition for backup five minutes when Bona is healthy.

#2533. Sunday Night Football: Bears overcome five giveaways, beat Bucs 27-24

It was a wild one in Chicago, but the Bears were able to pull out a 27-24 victory over the Buccaneers and move to 7-2 on the season.

Caleb Williams and the Bears’ offense started out white hot, but an interception midway through the second quarter threw off the unit for nearly the rest of the night. Williams ended up tossing four interceptions — the most in a single game he’s had in his college or pro career.

But even with five giveaways — Luther Burden also had a fumble in the fourth quarter — the Buccaneers scored just 10 points off of them. Tampa Bay couldn’t turn a blocked punt into points either, despite getting the ball at midfield.

Chicago began the game with a 14-0 lead, as Williams tossed touchdowns to Rome Odunze and Burden. The Buccaneers got on the board with Chase McLaughlin’s 27-yard field goal in the second quarter before Cairo Santos hit from 25 yards to make the score 17-3 with 3:02 left in the half. McLaughlin drilled a 21-yard field goal to end the half, with Bucs head coach Todd Bowles explaining in his halftime interview on the NBC broadcast that he felt his team could score to start the third quarter.

That turned into reality, as Bucky Irving scored a 2-yard touchdown to cap Tampa Bay’s opening drive in the second half, narrowing Chicago’s lead to 17-13.

While Williams threw his fourth interception, Baker Mayfield then threw a pick of his own to Jaylon Johnson, who returned it 67 yards for a touchdown.

McLaughlin again made it a one-possession game with a 35-yard field goal with 11:24 in the fourth quarter. Then Burden’s fumble gave the Buccaneers the opportunity to tie it deep in Bears territory, with Irving scoring on a 6-yard run. Mayfield made the two-point conversion successful by scrambling up the middle to the end zone.

But even with the offensive challenges, the Bears got the play they needed to win it. Williams connected with Colton Loveland for a 38-yard pass all the way down to the Tampa Bay 16.

After running time off the clock, Santos sent the ball through the uprights as the fourth quarter expired for a 38-yard, game-winning field goal.

Williams finished the contest 22-of-37 for 279 yards with two touchdowns and four picks. Burden led with seven catches for 97 yards with a TD. He had to be examined in the sideline medical tent after his fumble in the fourth quarter and was subsequently taken back to the locker room for further evaluation.

Mayfield finished 18-of-32 for 243 yards with two picks. Irving had 97 yards on 20 carries with two TDs, plus four catches for 28 yards.

With the win, the Bears are 7-2 in the league’s best division — as all teams in the NFC North have at least six wins. Chicago will be on its bye in Week 10 before hosting the Saints in Week 11.

At 3-6, the Buccaneers will also be on their bye in Week 10. They’ll look to get back on track on the road against the Lions in Week 11.

#2529. 2026-27 NHL season predictions: Expert picks for Stanley Cup playoffs, champion and major awards this season

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Following a brief offseason and an expedited preseason, the 2026-27 NHL season has arrived. Before the puck drops on opening night, we have some predictions to make.

If this season feel like it's staring earlier than usual, that's because it is. The NHL is adopting an 84-game regular season, which just means more hockey for the rest of us. That also means a long and arduous journey to the Stanley Cup is ever so slightly more difficult.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. With that in mind, we logged our expert predictions for the playoff field in each conference -- and there were a few surprises -- before making our Stanley Cup Final selections.

We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. A healthy Florida Panthers side will slot themselves right back towards the top of the Atlantic, and a revamped Washington Capitals side should be able to make some noise in the Metropolitan. Besides that, I have six 2026 playoff teams returning to the dance in 2027.

Nivison: As much as I hate to go with chalk in preseason predictions -- because it rarely happens that way -- there's no denying the top dogs in the West. The Avalanche and Stars are the class of the Central Division, and the Golden Knights should pound a pitiful Pacific Division into a pulp. Things get more interesting behind those clear Cup contenders, and I'm projecting another significant leap forward from the Mammoth. I also think Macklin Celebrini will be successful in dragging the Sharks to the playoffs in his third NHL season.

Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. There are still questions in Columbus. Can Adam Fantilli be a franchise player at center? Is the forward group as a whole good enough to keep pace in a competitive Eastern Conference? Still, I am sure the Blue Jackets have a really strong blue line, led by Norris Trophy winner Zach Werenski, and goaltender Jet Greaves is on track to become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. The Sharks are a better team than they were last year, and with Celebrini entering his third season as a legit Hart Trophy contender, this team won't be fun to play against.

Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Dylan Guenther hits 50 goals. Dmitry Simashev asserts himself as a budding top-four defenseman. Anders Lee and Vincent Trocheck provide necessary veteran depth. Now open your eyes. Utah is your Western Conference champion.

Unfortunately for the Mammoth, they will run into a refreshed Panthers team that now has double-barreled Tkachuks. Last season, we found out that all it takes to stop Florida is to hope all of its key players miss significant time with injury. The long offseason was probably a blessing in disguise as it allowed the Panthers to get healthy, and that's bad news for everyone else. The structure in front of the crease will limit some of the volatility we saw from Jacob Markstrom in New Jersey, and Florida wins its third Stanley Cup in four years.

Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. The Hurricanes were able to overcome their demons and win the East before ultimately taking home the franchise's first Stanley Cup since 2006. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. After three straight seasons ending in the Western Conference Final, the Stars regressed last postseason, flaming out in the first-round to the Minnesota Wild. The Central Division will once again be a gauntlet, but I'm ready for Dallas to take the next step and reach the Stanley Cup Final.

While Dallas has continued to fall short in recent years, the Panthers have done the opposite. The Panthers made three consecutive Stanley Cup Final appearances, winning back-to-back Cups in 2023-24 and 2024-25. Last season, Florida's three-peat attempt came to a halt on day one of training after captain Aleksander Barkov went down with a non-contact injury, tearing both the ACL and MCL in his right knee. An offseason of healing for Barkov, and the rest of the banged up Panthers, has the team refreshed entering September for the first time in years. With nearly the entire 2025 Stanley Cup winning core still on the team and Brady Tkachuk added to the fold, Florida looks ready to win its third Stanley Cup in four seasons.

Nivison: Celebrini should have won the Hart Trophy last season, but for some incomprehensible reason, he wasn't even a finalist. This year, Celebrini replicates that performance and gets San Jose to the postseason to take home his first MVP award at age 20. Hughes posts a career year in his first full season with the Wild, and Spencer Carberry gets his flowers for winning the Metro Division after missing the playoffs last year.

Baumgartner: McDavid's ability to take over a game was evident nearly every time he touched the ice last season. His 24 points (11 goals,13 assists) in the final 14 games of the regular season -- without Leon Draisaitl in the lineup -- was one of the many reasons I put him No. 1 on my Hart Trophy ballot. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. Barkov is healthy and the frontrunner to win his fourth Selke, and Dahlin will have another strong season to take home his first career Norris Trophy.

#2528. Celtics make surprising starting lineup decision against Bucks

MILWAUKEE — Mike Conley will get his first start of the season when the Celtics face the Milwaukee Bucks on Sunday night. Conley, who has mostly been out of the rotation, played a season-high 11 minutes on Friday night against the Charlotte Hornets.

In his 20th NBA season, Conley is averaging career-lows across the board; he's tallying just 3 points and 0.3 assists in 7 minutes per game across three appearances. But, on Sunday night, he'll get a rare opportunity to see more extended minutes.

Conley, who has been a starter in the NBA for the majority of his career, told CelticsBlog before the season that he knew mentorship would be one of his important responsibilities while his on-court minutes vary.

"It's part of the job at this stage of my career," he said. "I understand it. I understand there's going to be a lot of times where I don't play. There's going to be some times where I'm needed. There are other times where I'm just needed to be the voice for a big stretch of the season. Being comfortable with that, and being able to own that, is my role and my job."

And, while Conley hasn't played much so far, he has been a crucial voice in the locker room, particularly to Payton Pritchard, who has routinely asked him questions throughout the season.

"As somebody that's looked up to Mike, [I ask him] how he thinks of the game and how he was able to create his shots and create shots for his teammates and maybe handle playing the point guard position, momentum swings," Pritchard said. "He's been in a lot of great environments, great playoff series. How was he able to kill in those moments and dominate the game?"

The Celtics' most popular starting lineup this season has been Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta. That group started Friday night in a 119-80 win over the Charlotte Hornets.

But Joe Mazzulla has tinkered with the starting lineup quite a bit; Hugo Gonzalez started 3 games in place of Walsh, while Sam Hauser and Baylor Scheierman have each gotten one start this season. Mitchell Robinson started the first five games of the season before Queta established himself as the team's starting center.

The three guys who have mostly found themselves out of the regular rotation are Conley, Chris Cenac Jr., and Ron Harper Jr. Cenac Jr. is currently with the Maine Celtics, and Conley will get his first start of the season.

#2527. Kyle Larson, Cliff Daniels and the Hendrick 5 are who we say they are

When you combine the essence of Jeff Gordon, Tony Stewart, Ray Evernham, Chad Knaus and Jimmie Johnson, you basically get the Hendrick Motorsports No. 5 team, which is now doing a little bit of all the greats that came before.

Like, what else can you possibly say about Kyle Larson, Cliff Daniels, Tyler Monn, Jesse Saunders and everyone who touches this generation's Hendrick Motorsports blue car in some tangible way?

This is now undisputably and intangibly their era.

Larson has the versatility of Stewart. He is now one championship away from Gordon. He is practically on pace with Johnson. He has his own version of Knaus and Evernham in Daniels.

And by gosh, he has all the resources of Rick Hendrick at his disposal, and a championship format that once again rewards greatness in its various forms.

"Tony Stewart and Jeff Gordon are the two guys I looked up to through growing up dirt racing and stuff," Larson said. "To join Tony is such a cool feeling. I can't really believe that I'm on a list with him in championships.

"Winning races or similar races I could believe, but three championships and joining him is pretty amazing. Ultimately if I could join Jeff Gordon, that would be amazing also for a lot of the same reasons.

"Yeah, I mean, you want to just keep winning. Hopefully we can get there. I think Jeff thinks that I want to beat him and win five or win more than him. Obviously, yeah, that would be great. But for me just to be on a list with Jeff Gordon would be pretty awesome."

It's not that Gordon is encouraging Larson to surpass him. He is already resigned to it. And in the same way he was resigned to Johnson doing in a car he co-owned with Hendrick, Gordon stands to reap the benefits of this endeavor too.

"He's special," Gordon said. "It was one of the first things that I said to him when I saw him today. All right, there you go, number three, one more to go.

"I was on the other side of the Jimmie five-in-a-row championships. The way you do that is, one, you out-team him. You win the ones you're not supposed to win and then you win the ones you are supposed to win. In my opinion, that was last year and this year. "

This year, Larson entered the Chase as the winless seven seed who was 55 points behind top-seeded Denny Hamlin. They responded by winning three times, including in a step on their throats fashion response to a disaster of a Phoenix race, at Talladega.

Gordon lived that as a driver several times, most notably in 2007.

"That's what Jimmie and Chad did," Gordon said. "I think there were championships, honestly, at least one of 'em, I felt like we should have beat 'em. Man, they never quit. They never gave up. They came back and showed you how good they are and stepped it up and took it to another level. You're like in awe of it.

"I think that's what the competitors are looking at with Cliff and Kyle, that 5 team. They're in awe of things they're capable of doing."

This time, it was longtime rival Christopher Bell and longtime friend Denny Hamlin who played the role of a defeated Jeff Gordon. All they could do was acknowledge the greatness.

"I mean just an exceptional talent," Hamlin said. "I went through this generation's Jimmie, I think that's the only way you can describe it. When it comes to playoff time, they perform their best. That's something that Jimmie used to do. Jimmie was a guy that could get tons of speed out of the car. Kyle is the same, you could argue even more speed. There's a little more variance in the results because of how hard he pushes it, but he reaps the benefit because he gets lots of wins. That's something where he's going to be winning championships and races long after I'm gone."

Bell has been racing Larson for the entirety of their lives from Midgets and Sprint Cars to the NASCAR Cup Series. Bell has had his moments but Larson has enjoyed more of these moments on Sunday afternoons.

"He earned it," Bell said. "I think if you ask anyone in the crowd, anyone in the industry who the champion should have been, it's him. I love how (The Chase) went. I'm obviously disappointed in myself, but I thought The Chase was amazing. It delivered high-intensity moments throughout the entire 10 races – not just in the big shebang at the end."

For his part, Larson isn't even entertaining questions about the seven championships target, a par that would match Johnson, Richard Petty and Dale Earnhardt.

"I'd have to win five in a row to feel like I have enough time probably, like Jimmie did," Larson said with a chuckle. "Seven is a big number. These championships are extremely hard to come by. I mean, now that we're back to the Chase format, I think championships could be a little bit more realistic because it's not down to one race.

"But I don't know. Right now I'm definitely not thinking about seven. I'm happy to have three. If I could get one more, I would be even happier. If you end up getting four, then the next is five."

Larson said he appreciates the comparisons and compliments, and says Johnson himself has supported him and Daniels throughout the Chase, having personal relationships with both of them.

Daniels was Johnson's final crew chief and a lead engineer under Knaus. Larson inherited that team after Johnson's retirement.

"That's definitely gone a long way," Larson said. "It meant a lot. So yeah, I appreciate all that he's meant to Hendrick Motorsports and to Cliff Daniels and also shaping him probably into what he is today.

#2525. The Winners and Losers from Chiefs’ big win over the Jets

Your Kansas City Chiefs finally got back in the win column after taking care of the New York Jets 35-12 at Arrowhead on Sunday. The beginning was as ugly as it gets, and there were some ball security issues and short-yardage challenges. But the home team eventually remembered how to put together a complete game. They ran the ball, played great defense, limited penalties, and Mahomes got the ball into the hands of playmakers to rack up the YAC. That's been the formula for each of the team's six wins.

Here are a few who stood out on Sunday, for better or worse.

Running back Kenneth Walker III: Ken had three touchdowns and 143 yards from scrimmage; the Chiefs scored 35 points. It's that simple: get Walker going, win football games.

Running back Emmett Johnson: Number 10 continues his hot streak, breaking tackles on every play and scoring his second career touchdown. The Chiefs appear to have a complementary back who can help carry the load without sacrificing explosiveness.

Left guard Kingsley Suamataia: Correlation may not be causation, but the fact is that Kingsley was back as a starter on the same day both running backs made the winners list. He put some highlights on film against the Jets in the run game and on screens— especially the Kenneth Walker touchdown. Maybe having the starting left guard in the game is a good idea.

Defensive end George Karlaftis: George stayed Furious on Sunday— he was everywhere, with two sacks, six tackles and a pass defended. Three of those tackles were for a loss, forcing the Jets offense to (literally) go backward in the third quarter. Honorable mention to Ashton Gillotte, who also had a solid game and a quarterback sack.

Defensive lineman Chris Jones: The CEO is back in the office— it wasn't just the two sacks, but there was a different level of pocket-crushing and explosion this week than we've seen. Chris Jones got to the quarterback from the inside and the outside, had a tackle for loss, and a batted pass. This defense works so much better when he's using offensive guards for sleds.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: It was a solid day for Mahomes — 23-of-31 for 242 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. But it's the toughness that people will remember from this game. Somehow, after getting his throwing arm mangled on a strip sack, he didn't miss a play. He went on to lead multiple touchdown drives and take multiple big hits without concern for his body.

Tight end Travis Kelce: With question marks all over the wide receiver room and a disastrous start to this game, Mahomes went back to old reliable. Kelce delivered on four catches for 72 yards and a touchdown, including a 38-yard catch-and-run.

The QB sneak: One attempt, one fumble, zero first downs, one snarky Head Coach in the postgame— it's a 90% or better chance of converting for most teams. Why is this so difficult for the Chiefs?

Quarterback Justin Fields, Center Creed Humphrey, Kick returner Cyrus Allen: Each of these guys was responsible for a fumble this week. Along with the two strip sacks of Mahomes, that makes five times the Chiefs put the ball on the ground. Luckily, they recovered four — but the sloppy play started on the opening kickoff and could have cost them the game.

Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: Another injury on an otherwise decent day. Worthy finished with six catches for 48 yards before leaving with a hamstring injury. It wasn't a great sign that the Chiefs were reportedly desperate for a wide receiver before— they may want to add more than one now.

Kicker Harrison Butker: The Chiefs didn't need field goals to win this one, but Butker missed his only attempt — twice. He was predictably wide right from 56, then from 51 after a Jets penalty. The team would actually lose some available cap space if they were to cut their highly compensated kicker, but perhaps it would be worth the investment.

Note: Applying the labels "losers" is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It's just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.

#2520. Austin Reaves leads Luka-less Lakers to road win over Pistons

The Lakers controlled most of Sunday afternoon's game against the Pistons, including withstanding a furious rally in the second half to pick up a big road win, 121-116.

The purple and gold were without Luka Dončić for the contest as he was ruled out on Sunday morning with lower back tightness. Still, the team set the tone from the start and jumped out to a big lead in the first.

Detroit steadily chipped away at the lead before flying back into the contest in the fourth quarter with a big run with Austin Reaves on the bench. From there, it was a tight affair to the final buzzer.

LA finished with 16 turnovers but scored 23 points off Detroit's 13 turnovers. They also outscored the Pistons 58-46 in the paint with many of those points from Detroit coming in garbage time.

LA got off to a solid start with Matisse Thybulle stealing the ball, leading to Austin Reaves converting a layup. Thybulle was also left wide open under the basket for an easy two points. Los Angeles continued their strong start, going on an 8-0 scoring run that featured two triples from Quentin Grimes.

Grimes and Austin Reaves combined for 14 points.

The Lakers built a 14-point lead. Detroit was shooting 26% from the field. LA scored 14 points off the Pistons' seven turnovers.

An incredible quarter ended with Los Angeles getting help from each player who checked in. Sandro Mamukelashvili had five points and Ziaire Williams had eight off the bench. Grimes was in double figures with 10.

Jarred Vanderbilt grabbed six rebounds and dished two dimes. The purple and gold were up by 24 at the end of the first.

Detroit woke up offensively to start the second period. Daniss Jenkins and Kevin Huerter combined for nine points, slowly chipping away at LA's lead. The Pistons had taken over the momentum, shooting 42% from the field, while the Lakers sh-ot 21%.

Los Angeles' 26-point lead dwindled to 12.

Williams was a bright spot for LA. With Luka Dončić out, he and Grimes were stepping up with 11 points each. Los Angeles' suffocating defense from the first quarter had evaporated as they continued to leave Jenkins open for triples.

It was a Jenkins takeover as he ended the quarter with 22 points and was 6-7 from behind the arc. The Lakers weathered the storm enough to lead by 12 at halftime.

Momentum reversed again with LA starting the third period, building on their lead once more on the shoulders of Reaves. Reaves scored 13 points, pushing his total to an insane 32.

Huerter tried to keep the Pistons in it with back-to-back buckets. Cade Cunningham also saw the ball go in the basket, scoring four points.

It was all Reaves, though. He helped put the Lakers up by 17 with 6:30 left in the quarter. Detroit responded with Jenkins and Duncan Robinson each draining triples. The Pistons were outscoring LA 25-23 in the quarter.

Things took an absolute turn for the worse for the purple and gold as they fell apart and allowed Detroit to go on an 11-0 scoring run.

Collin Sexton restored some order for LA, scoring four in a row to put them up by seven at the end of the third.

The final frame was all Pistons early as they tied the game on the shoulders of Jenkins, who continued to shoot ridiculous from behind the arc. He was 8-13 from three and had 28 points.

For Los Angeles, Sexton was feeling it, scoring four points, helping put the Lakers back up. It was a three-point game with 6:59 left.

Crunch time became a back-and-forth affair as the teams traded baskets. Detroit made it a one-point game, but Williams responded by draining a triple. Jake LaRavia further extended the lead with a pair of free throws.

Robinson then made it a three-point game with 3:16 left.

The Lakers answered the call with Reaves, Kessler and Williams taking over the scoring duties, combining for 10 points, including a massive three from Reaves in the final minute.

Sexton had seemingly put the game away with free throws, but fouled Jenkins on the other end from behind the arc. Jenkins made all three free throws to make it a four-point game with 26 seconds left.

Sexton rectified the situation with two free throws. Detroit played the foul game and fouled Reaves, who then iced the win with a pair of free throws.

Reaves finished with 41 points, five rebounds and four assists. Kessler ended with 12 points, 16 rebounds, four assists and three blocks.

Grimes pitched in with 12 points and four assists. Williams had a stellar showing off the bench with 17 points. Vanderbilt did the dirty work with 10 rebounds and three dimes.

Mamu logged seven points. Sexton scored 17 points.

The Lakers' next game will be against the Atlanta Hawks on Monday at 4:00 PM PT.

#2519. Winners and Losers from the Seahawks’ latest sweep of Cardinals

The Seattle Seahawks did what they had to do to get the W against the Arizona Cardinals. Fireworks were not needed on offense, while the undermanned defense held down the Cardinals offense after the opening drive. The dominance over Arizona continues, but there a far more big picture things to focus on beyond winning 11 in a row over arguably the most hapless franchise in the NFL.

It's time for Winners and Losers from Seahawks 17, Cardinals 3!

An undermanned defense steps up to the task

Biggest winner for me was the defense, which took a kick in the teeth after giving up some big plays last week against the Chicago Bears. I know the Cardinals offense is bad when they're not playing the Dallas Cowboys defense, but the Seahawks gave up an 89-yard drive to start the game and didn't even let the Cards finish with 200 total yards. Sub-4 yards-per-play is excellent, and it's not their fault that two perfectly fine turnovers were ruled out because of substandard officiating.

Dante Fowler stepped up and got his first sack as a Seahawk, Byron Murphy II and DeMarcus Lawrence also got to Gardner Minshew, Derick Hall had three TFLs, Devon Witherspoon was a menace at the line of scrimmage, and Nick Emmanwori had a strong bounce-back performance after struggling versus Chicago. Above all else, this defense finally got some red zone stops, and perhaps it's fitting that they got the red zone issues "fixed" for a day on both sides of the ball.

It's not like Barner was the focal point of the Seahawks passing offense, but he caught his first touchdown of the season and turned three Barnyard sneaks into first downs and/or a touchdown. It's the second multi-TD game of Barner's career, and all of his touchdowns this season have come against Arizona.

The fact that Seattle had Barnyard opportunities in itself was a relief and a sight for sore eyes.

Drew Lock plays through pain, doesn't turn it over

It was a bit of a nervy start from Drew, but Lock gutted through the elbow and (later) oblique injuries to play mistake-free football. He wasn't flashy and didn't need to be, going 19/28 for 175 yards and a touchdown. Lock also scrambled for a first down and the only time there was a close shave on an interception was the screen pass that somehow got deflected to Cooper Kupp for eight yards. Also of note? No sacks.

This was, in a non-patronizing way, a high-end backup quarterback performance. Lock didn't do anything to put Seattle in jeopardy of losing the game, and made enough winning plays to get Seattle across the finish line. Now we wait to see if he plays in Week 10.

Zach Charbonnet gets closer to his old self

Seattle's run game wasn't anything spectacular, but when it was time for the hammer to hit the nail, Charbonnet was called upon. He finished with 77 yards on 16 carries, including a spectacular 17-yard run to help bleed the clock. His 25-yard catch-and-run was wiped out due to a really iffy Jalen Sundell personal foul, otherwise he'd be north of 100 scrimmage yards. Having Charbonnet get into gear should help the offense across the run, pass, and pass pro.

I can't really vouch for Price having an effective game as a runner (9 carries for 24 yards), but he had a solid kick return to start the game, and led the Seahawks with 54 yards receiving on four catches. Yes, Jaxon Smith-Njigba had just 51 yards on seven catches, which gave us the rare sight of a non-JSN receiver leading the team in yards. Price wasn't known as a receiving back in college, so this development was highly encouraging.

Offensive line holds up after some nervy initial moments

Lock was only hit three times and not sacked once. They got some movement in the run game albeit not consistently. Most of the pressures allowed were seemingly on blitzes and not four-man rushes. Some of the success I imagine is level of competition, but having your Week 1 starting OL + Josh Jones made for a calmer operation compared to the mess that was Monday night.

The Reggie Virgil catch not getting overturned for being out of bounds was astonishing, but that's on the replay center since they make the call. For what it's worth, I don't think Barner's touchdown was a catch but that's one that might have been too closer to over turn.

Deciding that Trey McBride's forward progress was stopped on his fumble was amazingly bad officiating and indefensible. The Josh Jobe DPI was ludicrous and made it seemed like McBride was a lightweight when he just fell down from marginal contact. Two turnovers taken off the board because of those calls. I actually don't have too much of an issue with the Devon Witherspoon taunting penalty, but having rewatched the Jalen Sundell unnecessary roughness I think that is a weak call. If it's not after the whistle then I don't think it was unnecessary roughness given Budda Baker was in the vicinity of where Charbonnet was tackled.

It was a flag-fest; yet another one involving the Seahawks. There were a lot of deserved flags on both teams, but this trend of the NFL over-officiating games has to stop.

Everyone knows A.J. Barner's touchdown celebration except Jonathan Vilma

Vilma was a great linebacker in the NFL and a Super Bowl champion. As an analyst? Yeah…

It was not an enjoyable broadcast to listen to, I'll put it that way.

Avery Smith is a liability on special teams

This is not a major thing when we're talking about special teams role players, but the rookie corner doesn't get on the field on defense (nor should he), so he has to show his value on ST. He's been culpable on a couple of big kick returns this season due to missed tackles and bad angles. Today was the second time he backed the Seahawks up due to a penalty. I wouldn't be surprised to see some healthy scratches for him moving forward once the Seahawks are healthier.

What is Emanuel Wilson's future on the Seahawks? The trade deadline is Tuesday. I can't pretend Wilson has much trade value, but he's been completely frozen out of the offense for two straight games. This week I am pretty sure he wasn't even part of special teams, which at least he was last week. Obviously the injury concerns regarding Charbonnet and Price are enough to not leave yourself thin at running back, but it's a bit unfortunate that Wilson has gone from a 100-yard game against the Kansas City Chiefs and a couple of other solid performances this season to an unofficial healthy scratch.

George Holani stays on special teams, but doesn't get any offensive reps. I'd say it's about time that happened. If you can trust Zach in pass pro, Holani still provides something as a special teams guy.

Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton get a little bit involved in the offense. A combined five catches for 59 yards for the other top receivers on the team. They each had successful third down conversions, which is a delight knowing how heavily Seattle relies on JSN.

JSN goes full Golden Tate. Please don't run backwards out of a first down again, JSN.

No strong opinion on Brian Fleury's play-calling. When you're down two starting offensive linemen, your starting QB, a starting receiver, and your backup QB is hurt, there's only so much you can do to make the offense functional. The execution generally looked better but this is a tough data point when assessing his future as OC. It was at least a relief to see Seattle stick with Price and Charbonnet and run more play-action again.

Beat the fading Raiders and you can get some much-needed rest. Klint Kubiak has the Raiders at least looking more competitive than they have been in the past couple of years, but the Raiders can't run the ball and their defense is arguably the worst in the NFL. Regardless of who the starting QB is, this game still favors the Seahawks and frankly I bet the crowd favors the Seahawks in Vegas next Sunday. If you get to 6-4 entering the bye, there's reason to believe in a late-season turnaround. There will be healthy bodies coming back, and the back-end of the schedule is not as daunting as it initially looked. No doubt the Rams and 49ers games will be tough, but the non-divisional opponents? Only the Giants (somehow, someway) could be a potentially scary one.

#2518. Blackhawks Sticking With Blashill & Staff Despite Disastrous Start

Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson is scheduled to speak with the media Wednesday afternoon, but isn't expected to discuss any changes involving Jeff Blashill and the coaching staff.

According to team sources, Blashill will remain the Blackhawks head coach despite a disastrous 4-13-1 start to the 2026-27 regular season, with the club currently riding a six-game losing streak. Assistant coaches Anders Sorensen, Michael Peca, and Mike Vellucci are also safe for now.

BREAKING: The Blackhawks will not make a coaching change and Jeff Blashill will remain their head coach ⤵️ https://t.co/JQokCEmojF

— Scott Powers (@ByScottPowers) November 8, 2026

The Blackhawks have fallen remarkably short of the preseason expectations through 18 games, with only four wins and the NHL's second-worst points percentage. With hopes of at least competing for a Stanley Cup Playoff spot in Year 5 of Davidson's rebuild, being ranked towards the bottom of the league in every major statistical category is beyond disappointing.

Goals scored per game? They're 31st among 32 teams. Goals against per game? 31st. Shots on goal per game? 31st. 5v5 shot attempts per game? Dead-last.

And it's not just the numbers suggesting the Blackhawks have been downright terrible. The eye test backs it up plenty, with TNT analyst Paul Bissonnette hitting the nail on the head last Wednesday while breaking down the tape against the Florida Panthers.

Bissonnette blasted the Blackhawks on national television, calling them a "soft" team and describing their timid brand of hockey as "Mickey Mouse" and "AHL-level". The former NHL enforcer told no lies, with the standard set far too low for Chicago.

Biz was very blunt about the Hawks:"I see a soft team… they don't really do anything well" 😳Then broke down their troubles with the help of the whiteboard pic.twitter.com/IWasxvqECJ

— NHLonTNT (@NHL_On_TNT) November 5, 2026

Then, just four nights later, the Blackhawks were embarrassed once again, getting pounded 9-2 by the defending champion Carolina Hurricanes on Saturday night en route to a sixth straight loss. It also marked the team's ninth consecutive road loss to start the season, with a 0-8-1 record.

The debacle in Carolina capped off a 0-3-0 Southeast road trip, with the Hawks getting outscored 18-6. Now back in Chicago with four days off before returning to action, the timing seemed right for Davidson and/or chairman Danny Wirtz to make a significant change, but it hasn't happened yet.

Ultimately, the Blackhawks elected not to go that route with Blashill right now, although it seems inevitable eventually, barring a drastic turnaround.

Instead, the coaching staff and management reportedly got together on Sunday to discuss potential adjustments and changes moving forward. Some of those changes could become clearer when the team returns to the ice for practice on Monday morning.

One has already been revealed, as backup goaltender Arvid Soderblom was placed on waivers Sunday. The Blackhawks later recalled Drew Commesso from the Rockford IceHogs, signaling a new No. 2 netminder behind Spencer Knight.

hi Drew! 👋roster moves 📰 ➡ https://t.co/kEjnCw2lNM pic.twitter.com/yuE73gJcZv

— Chicago Blackhawks (@NHLBlackhawks) November 9, 2026

#2516. Sights and Sounds from San Antonio’s Gold Cup early round win at Sacramento

The Spurs put together two of their finest wins during SEGABAGA road victories over Sacramento and Portland. When the NBA schedule came out, my sister and I reviewed which game that we'd want to go to, saw the airfare prices to and from Austin and San Antonio…. and concluded Sacramento made the most sense for both of us.

Some observations from an excellent night in the Golden Center:

The best comp that I could come up with was slightly slower and less athletic Allen Iverson with Jamal Murray's shooting range on offense. However, he and the rest of his teammates seemed lost on most defensive possessions, which resulted in quite a few paint points for San Antonio.

Not only were there wide swaths of the lower bowl that had empty seats, but there was entire rows in the second level that lacked humans, too. Though the Kings did themselves no favors by falling and staying behind by nearly 20 points most of the game, the ambience itself lacked the fervor of past seasons.

Things I saw in-person that I haven't noticed on the good ole television:

Luke Kornet seems 15-20 pounds heavier than last season.

Domantas Sabonis tried a lot of his bull-in-a-china-shop physicality on Wembanyama in the paint – something that worked well in earlier seasons – but found it no longer works for him beyond occasionally.

Dylan Harper (see highlights below) looked like the best guard out there.

Wembanyama suffered his infamous face-plant during game 2 of the first-round series and turned his ankle rather gruesomely on Sabonis' closeout tonight – so maybe I shouldn't be going to these games in-person anymore.

I'm sad I didn't get video evidence of Jordan McLaughlin's dunk attempt in the second half. It was impressive!

Chik-Fil-A rewarded its fans with a free appetizer if a Spur missed two free throws in a row, and this might have been the biggest win tonight in Sacramento…. with the exception that fans had to claim their victory a) in the app and b) before 10 AM the next morning. I'll take breakfast tacos anytime.

What started as a bad omen but ultimately was a big nothing-burger: the Spurs' rim was being repaired for over 20 minutes right after Wembanyama finished his pre-game prep, affecting the tip-off by roughly 15 minutes or so. Right before the repairs took place, I was impressed with Wembanyama's (mostly) in-motion routine instead of just practicing stand-still jumpers:

The audacity AND accuracy of Stephon Castle's re-direction here to Vassell in the first period will likely put this in the season-ending highglight rankings:

Speaking of Devin, this literally was a logo jumper late in the first quarter:

There were shades of young Tony Parker on this and-1 by Harper.

About $90 million of salary failed to box out Wembanyama on this follow slam.

Castle – for my more mature audience – is like a latter generation Dominique Wilkins with these two-footed lob jams on anybody and everybody

These simple two-man motions with Victor and a guard and shooters on the other side are good enough to win a lot of regular season games while keeping both the big man and his teammates happy. Devin's shotmaking ability late in the shotclock is exquisite.

On a personal note, this was the first chance to watch the Spurs in-person with my sister and her two kids since my dad passed. During the last Spurs game here in Sacramento on March 17, my dad suffered his last major fall hurriedly trying to get into his TV room to watch the game. My Kings rep Gavin was kind enough to gift us post-game free throws, and Shirley credited my dad for willing her free throw into the net.

#2513. Sri Lanka captain Mendis wins toss, sends a new-look Pakistan lineup in to bat in 1st cricket test

RAWALPINDI, Pakistan (AP) — Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won the toss and elected to bowl first Monday in the first cricket test against a new-look Pakistan lineup containing four players on debut.

Arafat Minhas, a spinning allrounder and player of the recent triangular ODI series, fast bowler Saqib Khan and top-order batters Tayyab Arif and Mohammad Taha were all on debut for the hosts.

Last-place Pakistan has won only two of the nine matches in this World Test Championship cycle that included its chaotic 3-0 loss in England in the last series and a 2-0 drubbing at the hands of Bangladesh.

Sri Lanka is ranked No. 7 in the WTC standings, winning just one of its six test matches while drawing three and losing two.

Mendis, who replaced Dhananjaya de Silva as test skipper in October, hoped his trio of fast bowlers will utilize the tinge of grass left on the wicket against an inexperienced Pakistan top-order as the tourists left out their front-line spinner Prabath Jayasuriya.

Sri Lanka has a recent happy memory at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium where it achieved the second-highest successful run chase in ODI history — 430 against England in the tri-series last month.

Veteran Mohammad Abbas will lead Pakistan's pace attack with express fast bowler Razaullah and Saqib. The home team also went without a specialist spinner.

Sri Lanka has been in Pakistan for more than a month, losing the T20 series 2-1 and the final of ODI tri-series to Pakistan.

Pakistan: Azan Awais, Tayyab Arif, Mohammad Taha, Babar Azam (captain), Saud Shakeel, Salman Ali Agha, Ghazi Ghori, Arafat Minhas, Razaullah, Mohammad Abbas, Saqib Khan.

Sri Lanka: Kusal Mendis (captain), Lahiru Udara, Pasindu Sooryabandara, Dinesh Chandimal, Kamindu Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva, Sonal Dinusha, Milan Rathnayake, Lahiru Kumara, Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.
